page.layout: One page of running text, with a margin note at the right edge beside the first paragraph. The left strip is the edge of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed. Running head at top, page number at top right, gathering signature and catchword at the foot.

main_text.p: solenne est iis qui se permittunt alieno arbitratu duci; eos sibi duces diligere, quos jam ante sci-unt duƥuros se in ea via, qua ipsi jam ante con-stituerant proficisci. Sic homines incautos Sa-tanas quasi circulo inclusos tenet. Si quæras, cur hoc putent esse verum & rectum, respondent quia ita nos docuit hic vel ille vir pius & prudens: Si quæras iterum qui sciant doctorem illum suum esse virum pium & prudentem? respon-dent, vel responderent saltem si ex animo loqui vellent, quia nobiscum sentit.——— {1}Et Sa-pit, & mecum facit, & Jove judicat æquo. Me-tiuntur nimirum plerique mortalium pietatem alienam, non ex praxi officiorum vitæ Christianæ, & ex operibus justitiæ, misericordiæ, charitatis, & devotionis; sed ex studio earum partium quibus se addixerunt, & earum odio quibus se inimicos profitentur,——— Κατὰ τὰς ὁμοιό-μιας τὰς ἰδίας ἑαυτῶν ἐπισωρεύοντες διδασκάλους inquit Apostolus, 2 Tim. 4. 3. Coarcervantes sibi-metipsis doctores secundum proprias concupiscen-tias: Κνηθόμενοι τὴν ἀκοήν, ut ibidem sequitur aptissimâ metaphorâ. Cum iis aures pruri-unt, quærunt sc. qui eas scabant, atque ita accidit eis quod veteri proverbio dici solet, Muli se mutuo scabunt.

XXVII, Tertiò, diserte nos prohibet sacra Scrip-ptura, aut alterius cujuslibet judicio conscientias nostras subjicere, aut in alterius conscientiam do-minium exercere. Ne vocemini Rabbi, unus est enim vester ὁ καθηγητής, magister, præceptor, doctor, ductor Christus, Matth. 23. 10. Ne multi estote magistri, fratres mei, Jac. 3. 1. Pa-scite qui in vobis est gregem Dei, ὡς ποίμνιον, ut sacem ei præferentes, verae fidei doctrinam & piæ exemplum, sed non ὡς κατακυριεύοντες τῶν κλήρων, 1 Pet. 5. 1. Non quasi exercentes dominatum

page.notes: Marginal note at right, beside "Et": "1 Horat. 2. Epist. 1." (mark 1 in the text). Greek passages (2 Tim. 4:3, Matth. 23:10, Jac. 3:1, 1 Pet. 5:1) are printed in a heavy, partly smudged face; the accents and some letters are doubtful and should be checked against the scan. Long s was normalised to plain s. The "Κνηθόμενοι" word and the first Greek phrase are read from a blurred line. The dash rules after "nobiscum sentit" and "odio quibus se inimicos profitentur" are printed as leaders and are kept as dashes. The line "Ne multi estote" begins a new paragraph by a number, so it is a paragraph, not a heading.
